text:
Side effects:

Astringency: 100% DMSO usually irritates skin on the upper half of the body. When the skin itches, dilute the DMSO with water or real aloe juice without added chemicals. Leaving 100% DMSO on the skin can crenate (shrivel) it, and the skin may take a week to look plump again. DMSO can also burn dry mouth tissue, so wet your mouth first.
Nausea: when drinking DMSO, dilute it in water, juice, or milk and sip gradually. Sensitivity varies, so try a small amount at first.
Reduced sleep: DMSO reduces how long I sleep when I take too much, take it too late, or use it over too many consecutive days. It builds up past a threshold that seems to differ between people, so it's best taken in the morning, and reduce the dose if you notice you're sleeping less. In rats, higher doses made sleep less deep. Some people sleep better with DMSO because it reduces whatever symptom had been keeping them awake.
Body odor: above a certain dose you may smell like sulfur. I don't smell when I put it into milk.
section: DMSO: Side effects (Mental Stabilizers That Don't Abort the Trip)

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?

question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone? Is each mechanism explained by what it does in the reader's experience (dopamine "for motivation (by showing us what is important to pay attention to)"; DeltaFosB "preventing that learning from really clicking"), not by where it sits or what it looks like ("a chemical blanket", "the slower one underneath")? (E375)
